translationRepairs: In year one, a gengzi year, the western tribes had already pushed inward and attached themselves to Dou Bin, great chief of the Moluhui.
In year one, a gengzi year, the western tribes had earlier invaded, so he had taken refuge with Dou Bin, great chief of the Moluhui.
依于竇賓 has Liwei as subject: he took refuge with Dou Bin after the western tribes invaded; the tribes did not attach themselves to Bin
Shenyuan ordered the tribal chiefs to Yinyuan to welcome the heir home.
Shenyuan ordered the tribal chiefs to Yinguan to welcome the heir home.
陰館 is the commandery town Yinguan; Yinyuan is a misreading of the second character 館
Kun gladly moved the populations of Mayi, Yinyuan, Loufan, Fanchi, and Guo south of the pass, rebuilt their towns, and ceded the vacated lands in full.
Kun gladly moved the populations of Mayi, Yinguan, Loufan, Fanchi, and Guo south of the pass, rebuilt their towns, and ceded the vacated lands in full.
陰館 is the county Yinguan; Yinyuan misreads the character 館

From the western hills of Pingcheng he studied the ground, then shifted south another hundred li to build New Pingcheng on the south bank of the Luo at Huangguadui, which Jin subjects called Little Pingcheng.

From the western hills of Pingcheng he studied the ground, then shifted south another hundred li to build New Pingcheng on the north bank of the Lei at Huangguadui, which Jin subjects called Little Pingcheng.
灅水之陽 is the north bank of the Lei River; 灅 is Lei, not Luo, and 陽 of a river is its north side
From the eastern Sushen Mohe to western Poluona, every people came in loyal submission.
From the eastern Huimo to western Poluona, every people came in loyal submission.
濊貊 is the Huimo (Weimo) people of the northeast, not the Sushen or Mohe
In the fifth month the chiefs met at Canhe Marsh to debate a capital on the Luo headwaters; after days of deadlock they accepted the empress dowager's counsel and abandoned the move.
In the fifth month the chiefs met at Canhe Marsh to debate a capital on the Lei headwaters; after days of deadlock they accepted the empress dowager's counsel and abandoned the move.
灅源川 is the headwaters valley of the Lei River; 灅 reads Lei, not Luo
In the nineteenth year's first month Liu Wuhuan died; his brother Kentou took power and plotted treason in secret.
In the nineteenth year's first month Liu Wuhuan died; his brother Etou took power and plotted treason in secret.
閼頭 is romanized Etou; Kentou is a misreading of the character 閼
In the twenty-first year Kentou's people rose; fleeing east, he drowned halfway across the river when the ice broke.
In the twenty-first year Etou's people rose; fleeing east, he drowned halfway across the river when the ice broke.
閼頭 is romanized Etou; Kentou is a misreading of the character 閼
When Kentou first rebelled, Xiwuqi and eleven brothers had been at court; the Emperor sent them all home hoping they would tear one another apart.
When Etou first rebelled, Xiwuqi and eleven brothers had been at court; the Emperor sent them all home hoping they would tear one another apart.
閼頭 is romanized Etou; Kentou is a misreading of the character 閼
Xiwuqi had by then stolen Kentou's host; Kentou, ruined, surrendered, and the Emperor received him as of old.
Xiwuqi had by then stolen Etou's host; Etou, ruined, surrendered, and the Emperor received him as of old.
閼頭 is romanized Etou; Kentou is a misreading of the character 閼
Former great chief Liujuan of Liang Penzi's line was Xian's chief plotter and knew the whole plan; he secretly sent Mu Chong to warn the Emperor.
Liujuan, son of the former great chief Liang Pen, was Xian's chief plotter and knew the whole plan; he secretly sent Mu Chong to warn the Emperor.
梁盆子六眷 means Liujuan, son of Liang Pen; Liang Penzi is not a name, 子 means son
In the seventh month the Kumo Xi chief Jiuji rallied the scattered and struck the traveling palace by night; cavalry ran them down and destroyed them.
In the seventh month the Kumo Xi chiefs gathered their scattered men and and struck the traveling palace by night; cavalry ran them down and destroyed them.
鳩集遺散 means gathered the scattered remnants; Jiuji is not a personal name
Returning to Niudie River, he raised a stele north of Ziyang Pass to record his deeds.
Returning to Niudie River, he raised a stele north of Guyang Pass to record his deeds.
棝陽塞 is Guyang Pass; the character 棝 reads gu
He sent Yuan Yi, Duke of Dongping, to open garrison farms in Wuyuan north of the river as far as Yusun Pass.
He sent Yuan Yi, Duke of Dongping, to open garrison farms in Wuyuan north of the river as far as Guyang Pass.
棝陽塞 is Guyang Pass, the same frontier pass named earlier, not Yusun
In the twelfth month he wiped them out; Qu Gou, Weichen's youngest son, fled to the Xueyu clan.
In the twelfth month he wiped them out; Qugai, Weichen's youngest son, fled to the Xueyu clan.
屈丐 is romanized Qugai; 丐 reads gai, not gou
Earlier Qu Gou had fled to the Xuegan tribe, and when the Emperor demanded him they refused to hand him over.
Earlier Qugai had fled to the Xuegan tribe, and when the Emperor demanded him they refused to hand him over.
屈丐 is romanized Qugai; 丐 reads gai, not gou

In the seventh month Xu Qian, Left Marshal of the Masters of Writing, urged him to take the imperial title; he changed the era name, raised the imperial standard, and began imperial progresses with halting attendants.
In the seventh month Xu Qian, the Left Marshal, urged him to take the imperial title; he changed the era name, raised the imperial standard, and began imperial progresses with halting attendants.
左司馬 is simply the Left Marshal; nothing in the source ties the post to the Masters of Writing (尚書)
On jiwei day he ordered Xi Mu, Supporting-the-State General, to overrun Jinchuan and took Murong Bao, Prince of Danyang Maidé, and others at Pingtao.
On jiwei day he ordered Xi Mu, Supporting-the-State General, to overrun Jinchuan and took Murong Bao's Prince of Danyang, Maidé, and others at Pingtao.
獲慕容寶丹楊王買得 means captured Murong Bao's Prince of Danyang Maide; Bao himself was not taken
That month the Xianbei chief Tufa Wuji took the titles Grand Chanyu and King of Xiping.
That month the Xianbei chief Tufa Wugu took the titles Grand Chanyu and King of Xiping.
禿發烏孤 is Tufa Wugu; 孤 reads gu, not ji
On guihai day Zhang Yang, Bao's Supporting-the-State General, and Xu Chao the Protecting-the-Army General surrendered the city.
On guihai day Zhang Xiang, Bao's Supporting-the-State General, and Xu Chao the Protecting-the-Army General surrendered the city.
張驤 is Zhang Xiang; 驤 reads xiang
In the seventh month Pulin sent Zhang Yang the Wuhuan with five thousand men to forage and raid Linghou.
In the seventh month Pulin sent the Wuhuan man Zhang Xiang with five thousand men to forage and raid Lingshou.
張驤 is Zhang Xiang, and 靈壽 is Lingshou, not Linghou
Generals Zhang Rang, Li Shen, and Murong Wen had surrendered earlier, then fled back; captured again that day, they were all pardoned.
Generals Zhang Xiang, Li Shen, and Murong Wen had surrendered earlier, then fled back; captured again that day, they were all pardoned.
張驤 is Zhang Xiang, the same general named earlier; 驤 reads xiang
On dingchou day in the second month the Emperor camped at Bozhi Hill in Julu, on the Hutuo River.

柏肆塢 is the fortified camp Bosi; 肆 reads si and 塢 is a fort, not a hill

In the ninth month He Lin, starving and cornered, led more than thirty thousand men against Xinshi.

In the first month of Tianxing year one, Murong De withdrew to Huatai; Prince Yi of Wei took Ye.
滑台 is the city Huatai, not a terrace

On wuwu day in the first month of year three the Skilled-Soldier General He Tu defeated Lu Pu in Liaoxi, captured him and his son Huan, sent them to the capital, and had them torn apart by chariots.

In the seventh month Qifu Qiangui was shattered by Yao Xing.

Fearing confusion among his ministers, on bingshen day in the twelfth month he issued an edict on success and failure, taking Yin-Zhou and Qin-Han as lessons, to guide his officials.

In the seventh month he ordered Zhangsun Fei, inspector of Yanzhou, to strike south at Xuchang and Pengcheng.

On gengshen day in the fourth month he again visited Mount Chai Palace.

On jiachen day he went to Mount Chai Palace and then to Green Ox Mountain.

In the ninth month he went to Nanping city and surveyed Yongnan and Summer House Hill, backed by Yellow Melon Mound, planning a new capital.
In the ninth month he went to Nanping city and surveyed Leinan and Mount Xiawu, backed by Yellow Melon Mound, planning a new capital.

In the sixth month he drafted men from the eight tribes within five hundred li to build the Leinan Palace with gate towers more than ten zhang high.

He enfeoffed Kui, son of the late Prince Min of Qin, as Prince of Yuzhang, and Yue, son of Prince Huan of Chenliu, as Prince of Zhuti.

In the seventh month he sat in Zhaoyang Hall, reorganized the offices, and personally chose civil and military men according to their talents.
In the ninth month he sat in Zhaoyang Hall, reorganized the offices, and personally chose civil and military men according to their talents.

He then climbed Mount Jiaoshi in Dingxiang and visited Horse City.

He went northeast beyond Stone Desert to Changchuan and visited Ruyuan.

On wuxu day in the twelfth month he made Liang, son of Prince Yi of Wei, Prince of Nanyang, raised Duke Lie of Yinping to prince, and changed Prince Le Zhen of Gaoliang to Prince of Pingyang.

In the fifth month Song returned from the desert; the Rouran caught them at Niuchuan and besieged them.

The court returned to Canhe Marsh.

In the sixth month Qifu Qiangui was murdered by his nephew Gongfu.

The Emperor went to Baideng and inspected the troops himself.

On jiayin day the Emperor went to Mount Baideng, reviewed the captives, and counted the stores of arms.

In the sixth month he went west to Wuyuan, hunted at Mount Guluo, and took a hundred thousand animals.

On jiachen day he founded the Temple of Xuanwu west of Baideng.
宣武 is the posthumous name Xuanwu and 白登 is Baideng

On dingwei day he hunted at Mount Sijia.
田 means to hunt here; 四岬山 is Mount Sijia

On jichou day in the third month Chuwen, Prince of Changle, died.

On gengshen day Xiu, Prince of Hejian, died.

In the twelfth month Liang, Prince of Nanyang, died.
南陽王良: 王 is the title, not a surname

On guichou day in the tenth month Kui, Prince of Yuzhang, died.
豫章王夔: 王 is the title, not a surname

That month King Wuzhao of Liang died.

In the fifth month he went west to Yunzhong, crossed the river, and hunted in the great desert.

In the third month Helian Qugai styled himself emperor.

辱孤山 is the place-name Mount Rugu

At Wudou City he feasted and rewarded his officers and men, held two days of public celebration, and gave out game as gifts.

On the new moon of the first month in year seven he went west from Yunzhong to Wudou City and gave his followers three days of public celebration.

On bingxu day in the third month Yiwen, Prince of Nanyang, died.
南陽王意文: 王 is the title, not a surname
On bingyin day in the sixth month he went to Yiyi Calf Mountain.
On bingyin day in the sixth month he went to Mount Yidu.
翳犢山 is the place-name Mount Yidu
On jiawu day in the intercalary month Prince Yinping Wang Lie died.
On jiawu day in the intercalary month Lie, Prince of Yinping, died.
陰平王烈: 王 is the title, not a surname

On jiazi day in the third month Xi, Prince of Yangping, died.
陽平王熙: 王 is the title, not a surname

He sent more than six thousand men from the capital to build a park from the old grounds east around Baideng, more than forty li around.
On yiyou day in the sixth month he toured north to Coiled Goat Mountain.
On yiyou day in the sixth month he toured north to Mount Panyang.
蟠羊山 is the place-name Mount Panyang
On yichou day in the third month Prince Henan Wang Yao died.
On yichou day in the third month Yao, Prince of Henan, died.
河南王曜: 王 is the title, not a surname
In the eleventh month the crown prince took command of the six armies on the frontier while Prince Anding Mi and Duke An of Northern Xin'an held the capital together.
In the eleventh month the crown prince took command of the six armies on the frontier while Prince Anding Mi and An Tong, Duke of Beixin, held the capital together.
北新公安同 is An Tong, Duke of Beixin

On bingwu day he granted a partial amnesty in Sizhou for all below capital punishment.
司州 is Sizhou, the capital province, not Jizhou

He sent Shusun Da, Marquis of Shouguang, and others east from Pingyuan to overrun Qing and Yan.

On wuchen day in the second month they built a long wall south of Changchuan from Chicheng west to Wuyuan, more than two thousand li, with garrisons all along it.
長川 is the place-name Changchuan

On jihai day in the sixth month Grand Commandant Mu Guan, Duke of Yidu, died.
太尉 is Grand Commandant, not Grand Marshal
His death edict had the booty Xi Jin had taken distributed to ministers from Minister Changsun Song down and to the soldiers by rank.
His death edict had the booty Xi Jin had taken distributed to ministers from Minister over the Masses Zhangsun Song down and to the soldiers by rank.
司徒 is Minister over the Masses; 長孫 reads Zhangsun

On gengzi day in the twelfth month he was given the posthumous name Emperor Mingyuan, buried at Jinling in Yunzhong, and his temple called Taizong.
